title: Exact Exposure-Map Specification Tests under Adaptive Network Randomization
banked_reason: D-0.5 cap-block: the main coarseness class assumes incident survival and essentiality close to its conclusion, and no primitive recognizable policy family or demonstrated design gain replaces that assumption.
gap_reasons: At the stated finite-table, procedure-defined faithful class, the proposal does not yet establish a field-scale consequence beyond certifying a partition; it needs primitive adaptive-policy families or a demonstrated design/practice gain.

The class assumes incident survival and focal/selector essentiality coordinate-by-coordinate, which are nearly the necessity half of safe-signature coarseness; replace or supplement them with independent primitive kernel/design conditions that imply survival.

The field-level novelty claim is unsupported until it is compared with variable-support/dependence algorithms for factor graphs, arithmetic circuits, and probabilistic programs, which may subsume the local product audit.
proof_attempt_summary: The run replaced an untyped compatibility-clique proposal with a typed finite-stage model, a local incident-product dependence identity, a width-parameterized extraction bound, and repeated-read survival/cancellation examples; this intermediate version briefly met the field rubric. After removing a definitional holdout theorem, review found that the main locally product-faithful class still assumed incident survival and statistic essentiality too close to the desired coarseness conclusion. A retry must start from a new specialization that derives those properties for a recognizable primitive adaptive-policy family and establishes a practical design consequence after comparison with adjacent symbolic-dependence literature.
tldr: The proposal asks when exact exposure-map specification tests remain valid after assignment probabilities adapt to earlier network outcomes. It repairs the model by typing stage actions, outcome availability, fixed policy and selector domains, nested exposures, and focal statistics. Its main proposed contribution is a local incident-product theorem: for positive exact kernels, dependence of a path probability on one response coordinate is determined entirely by the product of incident factors, yielding fixed-parameter extraction under bounded response overlap. A locally product-faithful class then makes the safe exposure signature the unique coarsest valid partition without schedule or clique enumeration, strictly beyond read-once policies; exact cancellation, incomparable-partition, and frozen-policy examples delimit the result, while schedule-specific holdout sets serve only as diagnostics.
gap: Existing adaptive randomization theory begins with a supplied conditioning rule satisfying q/S/T imputability, while network exposure tests use a fixed assignment law and static exposure graphs. The missing result is a typed, cancellation-aware structural criterion that converts adaptive kernel locality into a canonical ex ante partition.
fill: The project proposes the incident-factor equivalence and width-parameter complexity bound, a positive bounded-overlap faithful class with unique safe-signature coarseness, a repeated-read strict extension, a cancellation boundary, and a schedule-specific diagnostic for recording directly verified supported finer-exposure variation.
